name: getKeyStatus
description: Report whether this server is sending an API key and which plan the API sees. Use when calls are being rate limited or refused, or when the user asks whether their DexPaprika key is working. Takes no arguments and reads no market data.

name: getNetworks
description: List every blockchain network DexPaprika indexes, each row carrying its network id (slug), 24h volume, transaction count, and pool count. Read-only and keyless. Start here (or getCapabilities) to get the exact network slug that nearly every other tool requires as its 'network' argument. Use for 'which chains do you support?', 'is Base/Solana/Arbitrum covered?', or 'what is the slug for Polygon?'. Returns the full array with no pagination or sorting; takes no parameters beyond a short rationale. For platform-wide totals rather than a per-network list use getStats.

name: getCapabilities
description: Get the static agent onboarding guide for this server: supported workflows, network name synonyms (mapping words like 'eth' to the canonical slug 'ethereum'), recommended call sequences, and common pitfalls. Read-only and keyless. Read it once at the start of a session before your first query, or when asked 'how do I use this API?', 'what order should I call things in?', or 'which slug maps to eth?'. This returns onboarding docs, not live market data; for the actual list of network slugs use getNetworks, and for coverage totals use getStats. Takes no parameters beyond a short rationale.

name: getNetworkPools

The first page works without an API key; paging with cursor needs a key (a free key pages without limit). This is the primary chain-wide pool discovery tool. Use for 'biggest pools on ethereum', 'top trading pairs on Base', or 'most active pools on Solana'. Narrow to one exchange with getDexPools, or apply numeric/time filters with getNetworkPoolsFilter. Params: network (required slug); limit (default 10, max 100); cursor (pass previous next_cursor to page); sort_by (default 'volume_usd_24h', canonical *_24h fields, alias order_by); sort_dir 'asc' or 'desc' (default 'desc', alias sort).

sort_dir.description: OPTIONAL (preferred): Sort direction (default: 'desc'). The REST API calls this parameter sort.

sort.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_dir; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes sort, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

name: getDexPools
description: Get the pools belonging to one specific DEX on one network, e.g. all Uniswap v3 pools on ethereum. Proxies /networks/{network}/pools/search with a dex_name filter (the old /networks/{network}/dexes/{dex}/pools endpoint was removed): rows come back under 'results' with cursor pagination (has_next_page + next_cursor), and the 24h volume field is volume_usd_24h. Read-only. The first page works without an API key; paging with cursor needs a key (a free key pages without limit). Narrower than getNetworkPools (a single exchange, not the whole chain). Use for 'show me Raydium pools', 'top pairs on PancakeSwap', or 'liquidity on Orca'. Get the dex id from getNetworkDexes or search first, and pass that response's dex_id field ('uniswap_v3'), matched case-insensitively. Do not pass its dex_name field ('Uniswap V3'): a human display name returns HTTP 200 with an empty results[] rather than an error, so an empty answer here usually means the wrong form of the name was sent. Params: network (required slug); dex (required id, e.g. 'uniswap_v3'; the REST API calls this query parameter dex_name); limit (default 10, max 100); cursor (pass previous next_cursor to page); sort_by (default 'volume_usd_24h', canonical *_24h fields, short legacy names still accepted, alias order_by); sort_dir 'asc'/'desc' (default 'desc', alias sort). The old page number is gone: page 2 and above return an error pointing at cursor.

dex.description: REQUIRED: the dex_id field from getNetworkDexes (e.g., 'uniswap_v3'), matched case-insensitively. Do not pass that response's dex_name field, the human display name (e.g., 'Uniswap V3'): it returns an empty results[] instead of an error, so a wrong value looks like a real but empty answer. The REST API calls this parameter dex_name.

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of items per page (default: 10, max: 100)

cursor.description: OPTIONAL: Pagination cursor. Pass `next_cursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page (read `has_next_page` to know if more remain); needs an API key (a free key pages without limit). Replaces the old page number.

page.description: SUPERSEDED: the replacement endpoint is cursor-paginated and ignores page. page=1 (or 0) still works as the first page; page=2 or above returns a structured error telling you to use cursor.

sort_dir.description: OPTIONAL (preferred): Sort direction (default: 'desc'). The REST API calls this parameter sort.

sort.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_dir; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes sort, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

sort_by.description: OPTIONAL (preferred): Field to sort by (default: 'volume_usd_24h'). Prefer the canonical *_24h names; short legacy names such as volume_usd are still accepted and normalized. The REST API calls this parameter order_by.

order_by.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_by; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes order_by, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

name: getNetworkPoolsFilter
description: Get pools on one network filtered by numeric thresholds, returned under 'results' with has_next_page and next_cursor. Read-only. Use for 'pools over $1M liquidity on Base', 'pools created in the last 24h', or 'high-volume low-liquidity pairs'. Without a Dev plan or higher (a Dev, Pro or Enterprise key on api-pro.dexpaprika.com), pools created in the last hour are left out, so a created_after window shorter than an hour comes back empty. Optional filters (AND-combined): volume_24h_min/max, volume_7d_min/max, liquidity_usd_min/max, txns_24h_min, created_after/created_before (a relative offset such as '-24h', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD). Also network (required); limit (default 50, max 100); cursor to page; sort_by (default 'volume_usd_24h', alias order_by); sort_dir asc/desc (default 'desc', alias sort).

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of items per page (default: 50, max: 100)

cursor.description: OPTIONAL: Pagination cursor. Pass `next_cursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page; needs an API key (a free key pages without limit). Replaces the old page number.

liquidity_usd_max.description: OPTIONAL: Maximum pool liquidity in USD

txns_24h_min.description: OPTIONAL: Minimum number of transactions in 24h

price_change_percentage_24h_min.description: OPTIONAL: Minimum 24h price change, in percent. Negatives are allowed, so -20 finds pools down at least 20%.

price_change_percentage_24h_max.description: OPTIONAL: Maximum 24h price change, in percent

price_change_percentage_48h_min.description: OPTIONAL: Minimum 48h price change, in percent

price_change_percentage_1h_max.description: OPTIONAL: Maximum 1h price change, in percent

price_change_percentage_5m_min.description: OPTIONAL: Minimum 5m price change, in percent. The shortest window we carry, so it is the one to reach for on 'what is moving right now'.

price_change_percentage_5m_max.description: OPTIONAL: Maximum 5m price change, in percent

created_after.description: OPTIONAL: Only pools created at or after this time: a relative offset such as '-24h' or '-7d', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Without a Dev plan or higher, pools created in the last hour are left out, so a window shorter than an hour comes back empty.

created_before.description: OPTIONAL: Only pools created at or before this time, same formats as created_after (e.g. '-1h')

sort.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_dir; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes sort, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

name: getPoolDetails
description: Get the full current snapshot for one pool by address: its two tokens, current price, liquidity/TVL, 24h volume, and transaction counts, returned as a single pool object (not a list). Read-only and keyless. Use after search or getNetworkPools surfaces a pool, or for 'price/TVL of this pool?' or 'details for pool 0x...'. Returns live values only; for historical candles use getPoolOHLCV, and for the raw swap feed use getPoolTransactions. Params: network (required slug); pool_address (required, e.g. '0x88e6a0c2ddd26feeb64f039a2c41296fcb3f5640'); inversed (optional bool, default false, flips the token price ratio to token1/token0).

inversed.description: OPTIONAL: Whether to invert the price ratio (default: false)

name: getPoolOHLCV
description: Get historical OHLCV candles (open, high, low, close, volume) for one pool over a time range, returned as a time-series array. Read-only and keyless. Use for 'price history of this pair', 'hourly chart for the last day', or backtesting; for the single current price use getPoolDetails instead. Params: network (required); pool_address (required); start (required; easiest as a relative offset from now such as '-24h', so you need not know today's date; also Unix seconds, RFC3339 or yyyy-mm-dd); end (optional); interval one of '1m','5m','10m','15m','30m','1h','6h','12h','24h' (default '24h'); limit (default 100, max 1000 candles); inversed (optional bool, default false). History depth and interval depend on the plan: without a key, the last 24 hours at '1h' and longer; a free key (DEXPAPRIKA_API_KEY) opens 7 days at '10m' and longer. Asking for more returns 403 with a message naming the plan that allows it.

start.description: REQUIRED: Start time. A relative offset from now is simplest and needs no knowledge of today's date: '-24h' (last 24 hours, the whole keyless window), '-7d', '-90m' (units s, m, h, d). Also accepts RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'), Unix epoch seconds and YYYY-MM-DD (treated as 00:00:00 UTC).

end.description: OPTIONAL: End time for historical data, same formats as start (e.g. '-1h')

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of data points to retrieve (default: 100, max: 1000)

inversed.description: OPTIONAL: Whether to invert the price ratio for alternative pair perspective (default: false)

rationale.description: REQUIRED. 1-2 sentence rationale for this call (e.g. "User asked for X; calling Y to fetch Z"). Logged for MCP improvement, never shown to end users. No PII or secrets. See the server `instructions` field for the full convention and worked examples.

name: getPoolIndicator
description: Get a technical indicator (RSI, EMA, MACD, Bollinger Bands or VWAP) for one pool, computed server-side from the pool's completed OHLCV candles and returned as a time series. Read-only. Use for 'is this pool overbought?', 'RSI of this pair', 'MACD cross on the last candle', or as a ready-made signal input for a trading or screening agent, instead of fetching getPoolOHLCV and computing the indicator yourself. The indicator follows the pool's price as getPoolOHLCV reports it, with no inversed parameter. History depth and interval follow the same plan limits as getPoolOHLCV; asking for more returns 403 with a message naming the plan that allows it. Values come oldest first, one per completed candle: rsi, ema and vwap return `value`; macd returns `macd`, `signal` and `histogram`; bbands returns `upper`, `middle` and `lower`. RSI over 70 is commonly read as overbought and under 30 as oversold; a MACD histogram that changes sign means MACD crossed its signal line. RSI, EMA and MACD are smoothed, so start at least ten periods before the first value you rely on. Params: network (required); pool_address (required); indicator (required): 'rsi', 'ema', 'macd', 'bbands' or 'vwap'; interval (pass it every time: '1m','5m','10m','15m','30m','1h','6h','12h','24h' or '1d'); start (optional; a relative offset such as '-24h' or '-7d', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or yyyy-mm-dd; without it you get the last `limit` values); end (optional, exclusive); limit (default 100, max 1000); cursor (next_cursor of the previous page, not with start); period for rsi (default 14), ema (20), bbands (20) and vwap (14); fast_period (12), slow_period (26) and signal_period (9) for macd only; std_dev (2) for bbands only. A parameter that belongs to another indicator is refused.

interval.description: Candle interval the indicator is computed on. Pass it every time; '1d' equals '24h'

start.description: OPTIONAL: First candle. A relative offset from now is simplest: '-24h', '-7d' (units s, m, h, d). Also Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Without it you get the last `limit` values

end.description: OPTIONAL: End of the range, exclusive, same formats as start. Defaults to now

cursor.description: OPTIONAL: next_cursor from the previous page. Do not combine with start

period.description: OPTIONAL: rsi (default 14), ema (default 20), bbands (default 20), vwap (default 14). Not for macd

fast_period.description: OPTIONAL, macd only: fast EMA period (default 12)

slow_period.description: OPTIONAL, macd only: slow EMA period (default 26), must be above fast_period

signal_period.description: OPTIONAL, macd only: signal line period (default 9)

std_dev.description: OPTIONAL, bbands only: band width in standard deviations (default 2)

name: getPoolTransactions
description: Get one pool's recent individual swap transactions, newest first, returned under 'transactions' (paginate with page, or a cursor). Read-only. Requires a Dev, Pro or Enterprise key since 30 September 2026: set DEXPAPRIKA_API_KEY to it and DEXPAPRIKA_API_BASE_URL to https://api-pro.dexpaprika.com. Keyless and free keys get 403 (DP403_PLAN_REQUIRED); getPoolDetails still gives the pool's 24h transaction counts and volume. These are per-trade records, not aggregated candles (use getPoolOHLCV) or a summary snapshot (use getPoolDetails). Use for 'recent trades on this pool', 'who swapped in the last hour', or 'raw transaction feed'. Params: network (required); pool_address (required); limit (default 10, max 100); page (default 1, up to 100 pages) or cursor (a transaction id); from (optional, inclusive: a relative offset such as '-1h', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD; capped to the last 7 days); to (optional, exclusive, same formats, must be after from).

page.description: OPTIONAL: Page number for pagination, up to 100 pages (default: 1, 1-indexed)

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of items per page (default: 10, max: 100)

cursor.description: OPTIONAL: Transaction ID used for cursor-based pagination

from.description: OPTIONAL: Filter transactions starting from this time (inclusive): a relative offset such as '-1h' or '-24h', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Results always capped to last 7 days.

to.description: OPTIONAL: Filter transactions up to this time (exclusive), same formats as from. Must be after 'from'.

name: getTokenDetails

Read-only and keyless. Use for 'price and volume for 0x... on Base' or 'tell me about this token'. If you only have a symbol like WETH, call search first to resolve the address and network. For many tokens' prices at once use getTokenMultiPrices; for the pools holding this token use getTokenPools. Params: network (required slug); token_address (required contract address, e.g. 'JUPyiwrYJFskUPiHa7hkeR8VUtAeFoSYbKedZNsDvCN' on solana).

name: getTokenPools
description: Get the liquidity pools that contain a specific token on one network, returned under 'results' with has_next_page and next_cursor. Read-only. The first page works without an API key; paging with cursor needs a key (a free key pages without limit). Use for 'which pools hold WETH on ethereum?' or 'liquidity venues for 0x...'. Network-scoped, so run search first if unsure of the network; unknown addresses return empty results, not an error. Without a Dev plan or higher (a Dev, Pro or Enterprise key on api-pro.dexpaprika.com), pools created in the last hour are left out, so a token launched in the last hour shows no pools yet. For the token's own price use getTokenDetails. Params: network (required); token_address (required); limit (default 10, max 100); cursor to page; sort_by (default 'volume_usd_24h', alias order_by); sort_dir asc/desc (default 'desc', alias sort). Extra params such as inversed or paired_token_address are unsupported and error.

token_address.description: REQUIRED: Token contract address. Results are restricted to pools on the given network containing this token. Unknown addresses return empty results, not an error.

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of items per page (default: 10, max: 100)

cursor.description: OPTIONAL: Pagination cursor. Pass `next_cursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page; needs an API key (a free key pages without limit). Replaces the old page number.

sort_dir.description: OPTIONAL (preferred): Sort direction (default: 'desc'). The REST API calls this parameter sort.

sort.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_dir; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes sort, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

sort_by.description: OPTIONAL (preferred): Field to sort by (default: 'volume_usd_24h'). Prefer the canonical *_24h names; short legacy names are still accepted. The REST API calls this parameter order_by.

order_by.description: OPTIONAL: alias of sort_by; both are accepted. Not deprecated at the REST layer: api.dexpaprika.com itself takes order_by, so use this name when calling the REST API directly.

inversed.description: UNSUPPORTED: the replacement endpoint has no pair-perspective flip. Passing true returns a structured error; invert prices client-side (1/price) instead.

reorder.description: UNSUPPORTED (deprecated alias of inversed): passing true returns a structured error.

paired_token_address.description: UNSUPPORTED: the replacement endpoint cannot filter by a second token. Passing it returns a structured error; filter results[].tokens client-side for pair queries.

address.description: UNSUPPORTED (deprecated alias of paired_token_address): passing it returns a structured error.

name: getTokenOHLCV
description: Get historical USD OHLCV candles for one token over a time range, returned as a time-series array. The price and volume are computed across every pool the token trades in on the network (a volume-weighted price, and volume summed across those pools), not a single pair. Requires a Dev or Pro plan: set DEXPAPRIKA_API_KEY to that key and DEXPAPRIKA_API_BASE_URL to https://api-pro.dexpaprika.com. On a keyless or free key this returns 403 (DP403_PLAN_REQUIRED), since there is no keyless or free window at all. On that 403, fall back to getPoolOHLCV on the token's main pool, found with getTokenPools sorted by volume. Use for 'price history of this token' or 'USD chart for this token'; for a single pair's candles use getPoolOHLCV, and for the current price use getTokenDetails. Params: network (required); token_address (required); start (required; easiest as a relative offset from now such as '-24h', so you need not know today's date; also Unix seconds, RFC3339 or yyyy-mm-dd); end (optional, same formats); interval one of '1m','5m','10m','15m','30m','1h','6h','12h','24h' (default '24h'); limit (default 10, max 1000 candles). Dev plan history is limited to the last 30 days. There is no inversed parameter on this endpoint.

start.description: REQUIRED: Start time. A relative offset from now is simplest and needs no knowledge of today's date: '-24h' (last 24 hours), '-7d', '-90m' (units s, m, h, d). Also accepts RFC3339 (e.g. '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'), Unix epoch seconds and YYYY-MM-DD (treated as 00:00:00 UTC).

end.description: OPTIONAL: End time, same formats as start (e.g. '-1h')

limit.description: OPTIONAL: Number of data points to retrieve (default: 10, max: 1000)

name: getTokenIndicator

On a keyless or free key this returns 403 (DP403_PLAN_REQUIRED); then use getPoolIndicator on the token's main pool, found with getTokenPools sorted by volume. Use for 'RSI of this token' or a token-level signal for an agent; for one pair use getPoolIndicator. Values come oldest first, one per completed candle: rsi, ema and vwap return `value`; macd returns `macd`, `signal` and `histogram`; bbands returns `upper`, `middle` and `lower`. RSI over 70 is commonly read as overbought and under 30 as oversold; a MACD histogram that changes sign means MACD crossed its signal line. RSI, EMA and MACD are smoothed, so start at least ten periods before the first value you rely on. Params: network (required); token_address (required); indicator (required): 'rsi', 'ema', 'macd', 'bbands' or 'vwap'; interval (pass it every time: '1m','5m','10m','15m','30m','1h','6h','12h','24h' or '1d'); start (optional; a relative offset such as '-24h' or '-7d', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or yyyy-mm-dd; without it you get the last `limit` values); end (optional, exclusive); limit (default 100, max 1000); cursor (next_cursor of the previous page, not with start); period for rsi (default 14), ema (20), bbands (20) and vwap (14); fast_period (12), slow_period (26) and signal_period (9) for macd only; std_dev (2) for bbands only. A parameter that belongs to another indicator is refused.

name: filterNetworkTokens
description: Get tokens on one network matching numeric thresholds, returned under 'results' with has_next_page and next_cursor. Read-only. The first page works without an API key; paging with cursor needs a key (a free key pages without limit). Choose this over getTopTokens when the user gives numeric constraints or a time window. Use for 'tokens with FDV over $10M on Base', 'newly created tokens today', or 'low-liquidity high-volume tokens'. Without a Dev plan or higher (a Dev, Pro or Enterprise key on api-pro.dexpaprika.com), tokens created in the last hour are left out, so a created_after window shorter than an hour comes back empty. Optional filters (AND-combined): volume_24h_min/max, liquidity_usd_min/max, fdv_min/max, txns_24h_min, price_change_percentage_24h_min/max, created_after/created_before (a relative offset such as '-24h', Unix seconds, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD). Also network (required); limit (default 50, max 100); cursor to page; sort_by (default 'volume_usd_24h', alias order_by); sort_dir asc/desc (default 'desc', alias sort).
